html:
The capital of Penang in Malaysia, founded in 1786 by Francis Light of the British East India Company. It was the first British settlement in the Malay world.

Light got the island from the Sultan of Kedah, who hoped for British help against Siam and Burma, help that never came. He named the town after King George III and made it a free port, with no duties, to draw trade away from Dutch ports. Merchants and workers came from China, India, Sumatra and the Malay states, and the town grew into a mix of Chinese clan houses, mosques, Hindu temples and churches.

In 1826 Penang was joined with Malacca and Singapore as the Straits Settlements, but Singapore soon outgrew it. George Town stayed a centre of trade for tin from the peninsula and goods from Sumatra. Its old town, with its shophouses, was listed by UNESCO in 2008 together with Malacca, home of A Famosa.
sum: The capital of Penang in Malaysia, founded in 1786 by Francis Light of the British East India Company. It was the first British settlement in the Malay world.
